name: DraftSEO.ai
author: Kliment

sections.description:
Publish complete, AI-generated blog posts from DraftSEO.ai to WordPress in one click — or fully automatically. Images land in your own Media Library, SEO metadata is written to your SEO plugin, and categories and tags are applied. No copy-pasting, no manual uploads.

Key Features

  • One-click or automatic publishing — Send finished blogs to WordPress as a draft, a scheduled post, or a live post. Turn on Auto-publish to have new blogs published for you.
  • Images in your own Media Library — Every image (with its alt text and a short, descriptive file name) is downloaded to your Media Library in the background, with its smaller sizes saved as WebP where your server supports it — no external hotlinking.
  • You stay in control — A Settings tab lets you choose how the article title heading is handled and which structured data (FAQ, video, article) the plugin adds.
  • Works with your SEO plugin — The meta description and focus keyword (plus secondary keywords where the plugin takes several) are written automatically to Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, or The SEO Framework, in the place each plugin actually reads them. Your SEO plugin keeps control of the title template, canonical URL and social tags. No SEO plugin? The meta description is still added to the page.
  • WordPress excerpt filled in — Each article’s excerpt is its meta description, so blog listings show a proper summary instead of a cut-off first paragraph. An excerpt you write yourself is never overwritten.
  • Rich-result structured data — Adds VideoObject schema for embedded YouTube videos and FAQ schema — merged into your SEO plugin’s own schema where it has one — so your posts are eligible for video and FAQ rich results in Google.
  • Categories & tags — Syncs your WordPress categories and auto-creates tags from each blog’s keywords.
  • Clean, portable HTML — Proper heading structure, responsive tables, clickable in-text citations with a linked references list, and rel="noopener noreferrer" on external links.
  • Built-in activity log — A Logs tab records every publish and image import. Filter by type, search, export to CSV, or clear it out.
  • Self-healing images — Images import in parallel in the background, and a daily check automatically re-imports anything an interrupted job missed.
  • Secure by design — Your connection credentials are encrypted, and disconnecting or removing the plugin fully revokes access, so no stale connections are left behind.

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. In another browser tab, log in to your DraftSEO.ai account.
  3. Go to DraftSEO → Settings and click Connect with DraftSEO.ai — the connection completes automatically over OAuth (no API key to copy).
  4. Generate a blog in DraftSEO.ai and click Publish to WordPress, or switch on Auto-publish.

Requires an active DraftSEO.ai account. Visit draftseo.ai to sign up.

External Services

This plugin connects to DraftSEO.ai to generate and publish AI-written blog content. An active DraftSEO.ai account is required.

Data sent to DraftSEO.ai:
– Your website URL and a connection token (set up automatically when you connect)
– Publishing results for the blogs you choose to publish, with technical details that help diagnose them: the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions, the PHP memory limit, which editor your site uses, which supported SEO plugin is active, and whether your theme shows the post title as a heading
– A notice when the plugin is switched off, disconnected or deleted, so your account stays in sync. It says which of the three it was, the username and user ID of the WordPress user who did it, how it was done (for example the Plugins screen or WP-CLI), and the plugin and WordPress versions

Data DraftSEO.ai reads from your site, using the connection token:
– Your published posts, pages and product categories (titles, addresses, SEO descriptions), so new articles can link to them
– This plugin’s own log of warnings and errors (about publishing, image imports and SEO data), so DraftSEO.ai support can find and fix problems. It contains no information about your visitors

Data received from DraftSEO.ai:
– Generated blog content
– Images and their metadata

Service provider: DraftSEO.ai — draftseo.ai

sections.installation:
From your WordPress dashboard

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New and search for “DraftSEO.ai”.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.

Manual upload

  1. Download the plugin ZIP.
  2. Go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, choose the ZIP, and click Install Now.
  3. Click Activate.

Connect

In another browser tab, log in to your DraftSEO.ai account. Then go to DraftSEO → Settings and click Connect with DraftSEO.ai. The connection completes automatically — there’s no API key to copy.
sections.faq:
Do I need a DraftSEO.ai account?

Yes — the plugin publishes content from your DraftSEO.ai account, so you’ll need an active one. Sign up at draftseo.ai.

How do I connect my site?

Log in to your DraftSEO.ai account in one tab, then click “Connect with DraftSEO.ai” on the plugin’s settings page. The connection is made automatically over OAuth — there’s no API key to copy or paste.

Where do my images go?

Every image is downloaded to your own WordPress Media Library and served from your site, so you keep full ownership with no ongoing dependency on DraftSEO.ai. There’s no limit on the number of images per post.

What if an image fails to import?

Publishing never waits on images — the post goes live immediately and images import in the background. If a download is interrupted, a daily background check re-imports the missing images automatically, so there’s nothing for you to do.

Which SEO plugins are supported?

Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, and The SEO Framework. The meta description and focus keyword are written to whichever you have active (The SEO Framework has no keyword field, so it gets the description). If you add or switch SEO plugins later, the new one is filled in for your existing DraftSEO.ai articles automatically — only where its fields are still empty.

Does DraftSEO.ai change my SEO title, canonical URL or social settings?

No. Your SEO plugin already builds those from the post, and it keeps doing so. (Versions before 1.7.0 set a canonical URL; updating removes the ones they set, so your articles use their real address and appear in your XML sitemap.)

My theme shows the article title twice, or not at all. What can I change?

Go to DraftSEO → Settings → Article title heading. Automatic adds the title as a heading only when your theme shows none; choose Always or Never to decide yourself. It applies to all your DraftSEO articles at once.

I use LiteSpeed Cache. Are my DraftSEO images optimised?

Yes — every image is a normal Media Library item with all its sizes, so LiteSpeed Cache optimises it like any upload. To serve WebP versions, turn on LiteSpeed Cache → Image Optimization (including the automatic request cron) and Image WebP Replacement. Since 1.7.0 the smaller sizes are already WebP when your server supports it.

Can I publish to more than one site?

Yes. Connect as many WordPress sites as you like to your DraftSEO.ai account — each just needs the plugin installed and connected.

Does it work with custom post types?

Not yet — the plugin publishes to standard WordPress posts and pages.

Where can I get help?

Visit draftseo.ai/contact.
sections.changelog:
1.7.0

Full support for the five most popular SEO plugins — and your DraftSEO.ai articles back in your XML sitemap.

New features

  • The SEO Framework is supported — it receives the meta description.
  • SEOPress receives the focus keyword in its “Target keywords” box.
  • Secondary keywords go to Rank Math, All in One SEO and SEOPress when DraftSEO.ai has them for an article.
  • The WordPress excerpt is the article’s meta description, so themes that show a summary in your blog list show
    a real one instead of a cut-off first paragraph. Existing articles with an empty excerpt are filled in; an
    excerpt you wrote yourself is never changed.
  • Add or switch SEO plugins later and the new one is filled in for every existing DraftSEO.ai article — only
    fields that are still empty.
  • No SEO plugin? Your articles still get their meta description. It is added only when nothing else on the page
    prints one.
  • FAQ and video structured data now join your SEO plugin’s own schema (Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO,
    The SEO Framework) instead of sitting in separate blocks, and are skipped when your SEO plugin already
    describes the same FAQ or video.
  • If your theme shows no H1 heading on an article, the article title is added as one. The plugin checks the
    finished page, so themes that already show the title are left exactly as they are.
  • Images get short, descriptive file names (for example “oak-herringbone-floor-satin-finish.png”) instead of
    random ones, as Google recommends.
  • The smaller image sizes your theme shows are saved as WebP when your server supports it — usually several times
    lighter than PNG. The original image is kept exactly as it was, on every WordPress version.
  • A Settings tab. Choose how the article title heading is handled (Automatic, Always or Never), and switch FAQ,
    video and article structured data on or off.
  • Article structured data (BlogPosting) for your articles when your SEO plugin does not add its own.
    Password-protected articles are never described to search engines.
  • A Relinking tab. When DraftSEO.ai reconnects your articles — for example after a backup restore or a reinstall —
    and finds a post at an article’s address that it cannot confirm as its own, that post now waits in
    DraftSEO → Relinking for you to approve or reject. Nothing on your site is taken over without your say.

Improvements

  • Security hardening across the plugin, following the latest WordPress security guidance:
    • Every request from DraftSEO.ai is held to stricter rules — articles can only be created as posts, pages or
      products, with standard publishing statuses, and under an author who is allowed to write them.
    • The plugin’s internal article data is protected and no longer appears in the editor’s Custom Fields panel.
    • Images are only downloaded from DraftSEO.ai’s own image storage and your own site, over secure
      connections, in standard image formats, and within sensible size limits.
    • Your connection key is stored with modern authenticated encryption, connect links work only once, and the
      plugin only ever talks to DraftSEO.ai over HTTPS.
    • FAQ and video structured data are checked again before they are added to your pages, and
      password-protected articles keep their FAQ and description private.
    • Answers sent to DraftSEO.ai are marked so page caches never store them, and server folder names are left
      out of the plugin’s log.
    • Plugin log lines are only copied to the PHP error log when you have WordPress debug logging switched on.
  • The DraftSEO.ai menu is shown only to administrators — the people who can use it.
  • Log export opens correctly in Excel (accented letters included), exports exactly the entries you filtered, and
    is safe to open in any spreadsheet.
  • The plugin’s admin screens can now be fully translated, and the Logs filters work with screen readers.
  • Special characters such as “&” and “’” now appear correctly in article structured data.
  • FAQ and video structured data and the article styles now also apply to articles published as pages.
  • FAQ and video structured data are written so that no text inside them can break the page’s code.
  • When the plugin is switched off, disconnected or deleted, DraftSEO.ai is told which of the three it was, which
    WordPress user did it and how (the Plugins screen, WP-CLI, a site-management tool …), so your DraftSEO.ai
    account shows what really happened. The result is also written to the plugin’s log.
  • DraftSEO.ai support can read this plugin’s own log of warnings and errors, to find and fix problems without
    asking you to export it. See “External Services” below.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.1 and PHP 8.5. The bundled Action Scheduler background-job library is updated to 3.9.3,
    which removes the deprecation notices it logged on PHP 8.4 and newer. WordPress 6.2 is still the minimum.

Fixes

  • Articles published with images since version 1.5.0 told search engines their address was a temporary
    “?p=123” link instead of their real one, and Yoast SEO, Rank Math and SEOPress left them out of your XML
    sitemap because of it. The plugin no longer sets a canonical URL at all — your SEO plugin uses the article’s
    real address — and the old values are removed from your existing articles automatically after you update.
    Canonical URLs you set yourself are kept.
  • All in One SEO received nothing: it keeps its data in its own database table, which earlier versions never
    wrote to. It now gets the meta description and focus keyphrase, and existing articles are filled in
    automatically.
  • Image titles and alt text with accented letters, curly quotes or dashes were saved garbled in your Media
    Library — “egetru00e6” instead of “egetræ” — and so was the text inside FAQ and video structured data. New
    articles are saved correctly, and the images and structured data of your existing DraftSEO.ai articles are
    repaired automatically, once, after you update. Only text that is unmistakably damaged is changed — ordinary
    words are never touched.
  • A backslash in an article’s title or text was dropped when the article was saved.
  • On PHP 8, only one image per batch was downloaded in parallel — the rest fell back to slower one-at-a-time
    downloads and left temporary files behind.
  • Pressing Disconnect on the plugin’s page was reported to DraftSEO.ai as “plugin deactivated”, so your
    DraftSEO.ai account could tell you the connection would reopen by itself. It is now reported as a disconnect.
    If DraftSEO.ai cannot be reached at that moment, the plugin now tells you instead of saying everything worked.
  • On a multisite network, deactivating or deleting the plugin network-wide told DraftSEO.ai only about the main
    site. Every site in the network is now included, and every site’s plugin data is cleaned up.
  • In rare cases a very long article containing a video could be saved with an empty body. The article text is
    now always kept.
  • A stray closing tag in an article’s HTML could cut off the rest of the article when it was converted to editor
    blocks. Such an article is now kept whole.
  • The same article could occasionally be published twice when your site was slow or another plugin failed
    during publishing.
  • Articles with a custom or preserved publish date could be stored in the wrong timezone and end up “Scheduled”
    instead of published.
  • Switching the plugin off and on again stopped the daily image check and the log clean-up until the next update.
  • “Clear all logs” could fail on some hosts while saying it had worked, and log entries with unusual characters
    could be lost. The Logs page also showed the wrong retention period (it is 60 days).
  • Image imports: duplicate images on sites with a persistent object cache, a repair starting while an import was
    still running, and articles with many images on older connections are all handled correctly now. A scheduled
    article is no longer published early when its images finish importing.
  • Background tasks started from the WordPress admin run again with the bundled Action Scheduler.
  • Deleting the plugin left a few settings behind, and very large multisite networks were not cleaned up
    completely.

1.6.3

Clearer help when your web host stops this site from finishing the connection to DraftSEO.ai.

  • Improved: If your site cannot reach DraftSEO.ai while connecting, the error now says what usually causes it —
    a web host that blocks outgoing connections from WordPress — and what to ask your host for, instead of a raw
    technical error. On AlterVista, that means switching on server-to-server connections. The technical error is
    still shown underneath, for your host’s support team.

1.6.2

Fixes article formatting on ClassicPress, and adds ClassicPress as a platform you can pick in DraftSEO.ai.

  • Fixed: On ClassicPress, articles were published with block-editor markup in them — the kind of hidden
    comments WordPress 5+ uses — even though ClassicPress has no block editor to read them. They showed up as
    raw text if you opened the Text tab. Articles now arrive as plain HTML, exactly as the classic editor
    expects. Existing articles are unaffected; republish one to clean it up.
  • Fixed: DraftSEO.ai no longer appears in ClassicPress’s list of plugins that “use block-related functions
    and may have issues”. It never had a problem — it was only being counted because of the check above.
  • Note: ClassicPress 2.0 or newer is required. ClassicPress 1.x reports itself as WordPress 4.9, which this
    plugin cannot install on.

1.6.1

DraftSEO.ai can now link your articles to your WooCommerce product category pages, not only to your posts and products.

  • New: On WooCommerce stores, DraftSEO.ai can now see your product categories — their names, descriptions and SEO titles — so an article about trail running can link to your “Trail Running Shoes” category page. Only categories that contain products are shared, and nothing on your site is changed.

1.6.0

Articles now arrive as separate, editable blocks instead of one big lump — in the WordPress editor and in Elementor.

  • New: Articles are published as normal WordPress blocks, so every paragraph, heading, list, image and quote can be moved or edited on its own instead of sitting inside one “Classic” block. Sites using the Classic Editor are unaffected and still receive plain HTML.
  • New: Opening an article with “Edit with Elementor” now builds a proper layout — a container per section, with separate widgets for each heading, paragraph, list, image, video and table — instead of dropping the whole article into a single Text Editor widget. Nothing is stored unless you save, and your live page is untouched until then.
  • New: Images are linked to their Media Library entry, so WordPress can serve correctly sized versions and lazy-load them. This speeds up article pages for every site, whichever editor you use.
  • Fixed: If you design an article in Elementor, DraftSEO no longer overwrites your layout or deletes images it still uses when the article is republished. Only the title and SEO fields are updated.
  • Fixed: The daily image check and the repair job now also look inside Elementor layouts, so an article can no longer be marked healthy while still loading images from DraftSEO.

1.5.3

No more false “Out of sync” warnings — the plugin now checks with DraftSEO.ai before telling you the connection is broken.

  • Fixed: Refreshing the settings page straight after connecting could switch on an “Out of sync” warning even though the connection was working and articles were still publishing. The connect link is now cleared from the address bar as soon as it is used, so a refresh can no longer trigger it.
  • Fixed: Once that warning appeared, nothing ever removed it. The plugin now asks DraftSEO.ai whether the connection really is broken each time you open the Connection tab, and removes the warning when it is not. It also removes it automatically the next time DraftSEO.ai publishes to your site.
  • Improved: After you deactivate and reactivate the plugin, it checks the connection again, so the settings page shows the real state and offers a one-click Reconnect instead of claiming to be connected.
  • Improved: When a reconnect really is needed, the Connection tab now has a “Reconnect with DraftSEO.ai” button and a “Check again” button. You no longer need to delete your site from DraftSEO.ai first — your articles and settings there are kept.
  • Improved: Connection checks are recorded under a new “Connection” type in the Logs tab.

1.5.2

Articles that were still being prepared can no longer be treated as if they were already live on your site.

  • Fixed: When DraftSEO had to re-send an article after a slow reply, your site told it “I already have this one” — but not whether that article was actually published yet or still waiting for its images. DraftSEO now gets the article’s real status, so an article that is still a draft is never listed or shared as a published page.

1.5.1

Articles that got stuck as a draft now publish, and when something on your site does stop a publish, DraftSEO can finally tell you what it was.

  • Fixed: If the very last step of publishing failed, the article stayed an invisible draft and pressing “Republish” in DraftSEO could never rescue it — it re-sent the article but was not allowed to publish it. Republishing now finishes the job. It will only ever move a draft forward; an article that is already live is never taken down or changed.
  • Fixed: On hosting that cannot complete the normal publish step, the article is now published a second way that far fewer plugins can interrupt, instead of giving up after three tries. Its images are then brought over separately, so a slow host no longer costs you the article.
  • Fixed: An article that had actually published could be reported back to DraftSEO as a failure, because the report was based on running out of attempts rather than on looking at the article. It now checks.
  • Improved: When your site does stop a publish, the reason is now sent to DraftSEO — including PHP running out of memory or time, and how much memory your host allows. Previously every one of these failures arrived with no explanation at all and needed someone to read your server’s error log.
  • Improved: Publish and image responses now report your PHP memory limit, so support can give you an exact number to ask your host for.

1.5.0

Publishing now works on low-memory hosting. Articles are built quietly as a draft, images are brought over one at a time, and the article goes live only once it is complete.

  • Fixed: On hosting with a low PHP memory limit, publishing an article could fail with “There has been a critical error on this website” — sometimes succeeding one day and failing the next. Publishing now uses far less memory at every step, so it completes on hosting where it previously ran out.
  • Changed: An article with images is now created as a draft, its images are brought into your Media Library one at a time, and only then is it switched to Published. This means the article is never visible on your site in a half-finished state, and it never briefly shows images loaded from DraftSEO’s servers instead of your own.
  • Changed: Each image is now handled by its own background task instead of all of them sharing one. If your server is short on memory, the remaining images are picked up automatically by the daily check rather than the task being cut off.
  • Added: An image that fails is automatically retried once before it is reported as failed.
  • Added: A safety check runs every few minutes. If an image task is interrupted — for example your server runs out of memory partway through — it picks the work back up automatically. If images are still not finished after 30 minutes, your article is published anyway with the images that did arrive, and the rest are added afterwards. Your article is never left waiting.
  • Fixed: Turning the plugin off did not actually cancel its background tasks, so image and repair jobs could still run after deactivation. They are now properly cancelled.
  • Improved: Publishing no longer loads a large WordPress admin file it never needed, and it now asks WordPress for extra memory in the standard way — which your site can adjust.
  • Note: If you have chosen to publish as a draft or pending review, nothing changes — your articles are created with the status you chose, exactly as before.

1.4.1

Articles you move to the Bin are no longer reported to DraftSEO as missing.

  • Fixed: When a DraftSEO article was in your site’s Bin, DraftSEO could not see it at all — so it reported the article as no longer on your site, and “Reconnect articles” could not resolve it. Posts in the Bin are now reported along with their status, so DraftSEO tells you the article is in the Bin and simply needs restoring.

1.4.0

Removing and reinstalling the plugin no longer breaks the link to your existing DraftSEO articles, and articles that lost that link can now be reconnected.

  • Fixed: Deleting the plugin used to erase the markers that identify which posts DraftSEO published, while leaving the posts themselves in place. After reinstalling, none of your existing articles could be updated from DraftSEO again — every republish was refused. Those markers are now kept, so a reinstall picks up exactly where you left off.
  • Added: A new Re-sync tab in the plugin explains what breaks the link between your posts and DraftSEO, and takes you straight to the right place to fix it.
  • Added: A “Reconnect articles” button in DraftSEO re-links articles whose connection was lost — after a database restore, a site migration, or an older reinstall. It re-links a post only when the article’s exact web address still matches, and only ever one post per article — if two could match, or none does, it leaves them alone and tells you. Re-linking itself changes nothing on the post; it records which article the post belongs to, which is also what allows you to update that post from DraftSEO afterwards.
  • Improved: If you republish an article whose WordPress post was deleted or renumbered, DraftSEO now finds the current post automatically instead of failing. When it genuinely cannot be found, you are told why and what to do, instead of getting a generic error.
  • Improved: The plugin still refuses to overwrite any post it did not create — that protection is unchanged.

1.3.10

Articles are no longer reported as failed when their images actually imported fine, and you now get told when only some of the images made it.

  • Fixed: If another plugin on your site raised an error while your article was being saved, DraftSEO reported that every image had failed — even when all of them had imported correctly and the article was perfect. Your dashboard then asked you to republish for nothing. DraftSEO now reports what actually happened.
  • Fixed: One misbehaving plugin could stop the remaining images on a post from importing at all. Each image is now handled on its own, so a problem with one image no longer costs you the others.
  • Fixed: The same problem could make the automatic daily repair give up on a post permanently, leaving its images hosted outside your site forever. Repairs now check the post itself before deciding they failed.
  • Added: When only some of an article’s images import, DraftSEO now tells you which ones are still outstanding instead of reporting a silent success.
  • Improved: When an error does come from another plugin on your site, DraftSEO now records which file it came from, so support can point you straight at the cause.

1.3.9

DraftSEO can now see which plugin version each of your sites is running, so support answers are faster and you get a reminder when a site falls behind.

  • Improved: Your site now reports its DraftSEO plugin version, WordPress version and PHP version every time it publishes an article or finishes importing images. Previously that was only sent when you pressed “Test connection”, so when something went wrong on one site we could not tell which version produced it without asking you.
  • Improved: If one of your sites is running an old plugin version, DraftSEO now shows a reminder inside your dashboard with a direct link to update it.

1.3.8

Images now start importing the moment an article is published, even on a site with no visitors.

  • Fixed: Image importing no longer waits for someone to visit your site. Until now the import was queued and only started when your site next received a visit, so on a quiet site a new article could sit for hours with its images still hosted by DraftSEO instead of in your own media library. DraftSEO now starts the import itself, right after publishing.
  • Improved: If an import ever does stall, DraftSEO retries starting it every hour instead of giving up.

1.3.7

DraftSEO can now see your custom pages — services, projects, team members and more — so its articles link to them properly.

  • Improved: DraftSEO now recognises every public page type on your site, not just standard posts, pages and WooCommerce products. If your theme adds sections like Services, Projects, Team or Testimonials, those pages are now included when DraftSEO looks for places to link to.
  • Improved: Those pages now carry their real titles and SEO descriptions instead of a guess made from the web address, so links to them are far more relevant.

1.3.6

Image-import reports back to DraftSEO now say which post they are about.

  • Improved: When images finish importing (or fail to), the plugin now tells DraftSEO which post the result belongs to, and its address. Previously it sent only the numbers, so a failure showed up in your DraftSEO publishing history with no way to tell which article to go and look at.
  • Improved: DraftSEO can now fill in a missing post address for older publishes automatically when an image import finishes, instead of leaving the entry incomplete.

1.3.5

Housekeeping release: the plugin now leaves the rest of your site alone, does less work on every page load, and can no longer get stuck repairing the same post forever.

  • Fixed: The daily image check now looks only at posts DraftSEO published. It previously examined every post, page and product on your site and left a small DraftSEO marker on each one. Nothing was damaged, but it was untidy and slower than it needed to be — the check is now scoped to our own posts and runs faster as a result.
  • Fixed: A post whose images could not be fully tidied up could be re-checked every single day, forever. It now gives up cleanly after a few attempts, exactly as intended.
  • Fixed: When a background image job failed, the plugin assumed WordPress would automatically try it again. It does not. Failures are now either retried deliberately or reported and closed, so a post can no longer be left silently half-finished, and DraftSEO no longer shows a publish stuck at “processing”.
  • Fixed: If DraftSEO could not be reached at the moment an image import finished, the result was lost. The plugin now reports it through a second, longer-lived channel instead.
  • Fixed: A successful image import could occasionally be reported to DraftSEO as a failure if the network hiccuped at the wrong moment.
  • Improved: Background image jobs now run with a sensible time limit instead of no limit at all. A very large post stops cleanly and finishes on the next daily pass rather than risking a stalled job that repeats every few minutes.
  • Improved: Removed a setting that tried to control WordPress’s background-task scheduler. It used a name that scheduler does not recognise, so it never did anything — and had it worked it would have changed behaviour for other plugins on your site, including WooCommerce. Those settings belong to you, not to us.
  • Improved: Two database lookups have been removed from every page load on your site.

1.3.4

Video rich-result data is now complete, fixing the “Missing field ‘name’ / ‘uploadDate'” errors reported in Google Search Console.

  • Fixed: Posts containing a YouTube video now publish complete video structured data, including the video’s title, upload date, description, and length. Previously only the thumbnail and player address were included, which Search Console flagged as a critical error and which prevented the post from being eligible for video rich results.
  • Improved: If video details are ever unavailable, the plugin now leaves the video markup out entirely instead of publishing an incomplete version — no markup is better than markup Google reports as broken.
  • Improved: Republishing an older post from DraftSEO now upgrades its video data in place, so existing posts are corrected as you update them.

1.3.3

Failed image imports now retry automatically over several days and report a clear reason instead of a generic error.

  • Improved: When images cannot be imported (usually a temporary connection problem between your host and our image server), the plugin now retries a few times across the next days before giving up, instead of abandoning the post after one attempt. Republishing from DraftSEO still resets this immediately.
  • Improved: The plugin now tells DraftSEO exactly why an image import failed (for example an SSL, DNS, or firewall problem), so the cause is visible in your DraftSEO publishing history without digging through server logs.
  • Fixed: Manually published and republished posts now report image-import completion back to DraftSEO reliably, so a successful background repair no longer leaves the job showing as failed.

1.3.2

Republishing now respects your featured-image choice, preventing a duplicated image at the top of updated posts.

  • Fixed: Republishing a post now honours your “Set featured image” preference. Previously an update always set a featured image even when you had turned that option off, which could show the same image twice at the top of the post.

1.3.1

Refreshed light-themed admin design, faster re-publishing, more efficient syncing, and gentler default image importing.

  • Improved: Re-publishing a post when only its SEO details changed is now faster — unchanged content and images are no longer reprocessed.
  • Improved: Syncing large sites with DraftSEO.ai transfers less data.
  • Improved: More reliable image handling in post content, and oversized requests now return a clear message instead of failing silently.
  • Improved: Image importing uses gentler, safer defaults so it runs smoothly even on limited shared hosting, and activity logs are now kept for 60 days.
  • Improved: The settings screen now uses a clean, light theme on every site for a consistent look, instead of following the operating system’s dark appearance.
  • Improved: Modernised the settings screen — matched, rounded Connect/Disconnect buttons with smooth hover and keyboard-focus states, an underline tab indicator, a subtle DraftSEO.ai brand accent on the card, and a tidier single-column layout (with reduced-motion support).
  • Improved: The sidebar menu icon now matches the DraftSEO.ai brand mark.
  • Improved: Clearer, less repetitive wording on the connection screen, and consistent “DraftSEO.ai” branding throughout.

1.3.0

Security and reliability release: disconnecting now fully revokes access, salt rotations show a clear “reconnect” message, the connection flow is locked to the official DraftSEO address, publishing reports real success or failure, and the admin screens have a refreshed design.

  • Security: Disconnecting your site (from either DraftSEO or the plugin’s Disconnect button) now fully revokes the stored connection key. Previously the key the plugin actually used for authentication was left in place, so the site could still be published to after it showed as disconnected.
  • Security: The “Connect with DraftSEO.ai” flow now only accepts the official DraftSEO address, so a tampered connection link can no longer point your site’s connection at another server.
  • Security: Image and callback URLs are now validated to prevent server-side request forgery, and the completion callback can only be sent to the DraftSEO platform.
  • Improved: If your site’s WordPress security keys (salts) are rotated — by a security plugin, a host migration, or cloning to staging — the plugin now detects that its saved key can no longer be read and shows a clear “please reconnect” message instead of a generic “invalid key” error. Your settings are kept so you know exactly what happened.
  • Fixed: Publishing now reports a real failure if WordPress refuses to create the post, instead of occasionally reporting success for a post that was never created.
  • Fixed: Sync now also recognises articles published as Pages or products, so it no longer republishes them as duplicates.
  • Fixed: Background image, repair, and health jobs are now crash-hardened — a single bad image URL can no longer silently kill the job and leave “images importing…” stuck forever.
  • Improved: Faster sync on large sites (fewer database round-trips), tidier post URLs (native WordPress slugs), and accurate author names in the activity log.
  • New: The plugin now shows an “update available” note in its settings when a newer version is recommended.
  • New: Refreshed admin design that follows your WordPress admin colour scheme, with a clearer connection status card and a modernised Logs table.

WordPress 7.0 compatibility, plus automatic alt text from your images.

short_description: Publish AI-generated blogs from DraftSEO.ai directly to WordPress with automatic image import and SEO optimization.
description:
Publish complete, AI-generated blog posts from DraftSEO.ai to WordPress in one click — or fully automatically. Images land in your own Media Library, SEO metadata is written to your SEO plugin, and categories and tags are applied. No copy-pasting, no manual uploads.

Key Features

  • One-click or automatic publishing — Send finished blogs to WordPress as a draft, a scheduled post, or a live post. Turn on Auto-publish to have new blogs published for you.
  • Images in your own Media Library — Every image (with its alt text and a short, descriptive file name) is downloaded to your Media Library in the background, with its smaller sizes saved as WebP where your server supports it — no external hotlinking.
  • You stay in control — A Settings tab lets you choose how the article title heading is handled and which structured data (FAQ, video, article) the plugin adds.
  • Works with your SEO plugin — The meta description and focus keyword (plus secondary keywords where the plugin takes several) are written automatically to Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, or The SEO Framework, in the place each plugin actually reads them. Your SEO plugin keeps control of the title template, canonical URL and social tags. No SEO plugin? The meta description is still added to the page.
  • WordPress excerpt filled in — Each article’s excerpt is its meta description, so blog listings show a proper summary instead of a cut-off first paragraph. An excerpt you write yourself is never overwritten.
  • Rich-result structured data — Adds VideoObject schema for embedded YouTube videos and FAQ schema — merged into your SEO plugin’s own schema where it has one — so your posts are eligible for video and FAQ rich results in Google.
  • Categories & tags — Syncs your WordPress categories and auto-creates tags from each blog’s keywords.
  • Clean, portable HTML — Proper heading structure, responsive tables, clickable in-text citations with a linked references list, and rel="noopener noreferrer" on external links.
  • Built-in activity log — A Logs tab records every publish and image import. Filter by type, search, export to CSV, or clear it out.
  • Self-healing images — Images import in parallel in the background, and a daily check automatically re-imports anything an interrupted job missed.
  • Secure by design — Your connection credentials are encrypted, and disconnecting or removing the plugin fully revokes access, so no stale connections are left behind.

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. In another browser tab, log in to your DraftSEO.ai account.
  3. Go to DraftSEO → Settings and click Connect with DraftSEO.ai — the connection completes automatically over OAuth (no API key to copy).
  4. Generate a blog in DraftSEO.ai and click Publish to WordPress, or switch on Auto-publish.

Requires an active DraftSEO.ai account. Visit draftseo.ai to sign up.

External Services

This plugin connects to DraftSEO.ai to generate and publish AI-written blog content. An active DraftSEO.ai account is required.

Data sent to DraftSEO.ai:
– Your website URL and a connection token (set up automatically when you connect)
– Publishing results for the blogs you choose to publish, with technical details that help diagnose them: the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions, the PHP memory limit, which editor your site uses, which supported SEO plugin is active, and whether your theme shows the post title as a heading
– A notice when the plugin is switched off, disconnected or deleted, so your account stays in sync. It says which of the three it was, the username and user ID of the WordPress user who did it, how it was done (for example the Plugins screen or WP-CLI), and the plugin and WordPress versions

Data DraftSEO.ai reads from your site, using the connection token:
– Your published posts, pages and product categories (titles, addresses, SEO descriptions), so new articles can link to them
– This plugin’s own log of warnings and errors (about publishing, image imports and SEO data), so DraftSEO.ai support can find and fix problems. It contains no information about your visitors

Data received from DraftSEO.ai:
– Generated blog content
– Images and their metadata

Service provider: DraftSEO.ai — draftseo.ai
